action: Update iTerm2 to 3.7.9, which iTerm2's release notes say fixes the issue; Cyber Security News also advises not printing raw contents of unfamiliar files into iTerm2 until then.
date_note: Date is the day iTerm2 3.7.9, which carries the fix, was built according to its release notes; the researcher's write-up is dated 21 November.
exec: Developers and admins on Macs using iTerm2 could have commands run by viewing a crafted file; exploit code is public and a fix exists in 3.7.9.
geo_basis: no place is stated for the vendor or the flaw
plain: Viewing a booby-trapped file in the iTerm2 terminal app on a Mac could run commands. Version 3.7.9 fixes it, and the researcher has published code showing how it works.

key_findings: iTerm2 3.7.9 fixes a security issue where a crafted file displayed in the terminal could run arbitrary commands by abusing the Kitty image and drag-and-drop protocols.
Replies sent back to programs no longer include control characters that could be injected into the shell.
The researcher's write-up lists 3.6.1 – 3.7.8 as affected with default settings and includes proof-of-concept code.
Credited to Minseong Kim (@ii4gsp) of NSHC Red Alert Labs.

summary: iTerm2's 3.7.9 release notes, built on 20 November, say it fixes a security issue where a crafted file displayed in the terminal, for example with cat, could run arbitrary commands by abusing the Kitty image and drag-and-drop protocols. Researcher Minseong Kim of NSHC Red Alert Labs, credited by iTerm2, lists versions 3.6.1 – 3.7.8 as affected with default settings and has published proof-of-concept exploit code.
title: iTerm2 3.7.9 fixes command execution via crafted files displayed in the terminal; researcher publishes proof of concept

validation.note: Primary: iTerm2's own 3.7.9 changelog read in full. The researcher's write-up (ii4gsp.github.io) gives the affected range and a PoC; Cyber Security News relays both. No CVE appears on any of the three pages; none says the flaw has been exploited in the wild.

evidence.quote: The reported affected range is 3.6.1 through 3.7.8, and the flaw can affect installations using default settings.
Version 3.7.9 of iTerm2 was built on November 20, 2026.

review.note: Compared 20 Nov build date, fix wording, credit, affected range 3.6.1-3.7.8, PoC and no CVE/in-the-wild against changelog, write-up and Cyber Security News; evidence quotes found
